title: Claude built my own map animation tool
summary: I used to animate maps with GeoLayers: powerful, painful, and about a $200 subscription. Now I cut the A-roll, record voice notes like "map here, show the school", and Claude builds accurate maps from map tiles and satellite views with a small app it built for me. Here are the prompts.
steps: Run Prompt 1 once in Claude Code to build your own small map app.
Cut your A-roll yourself. While cutting, record voice notes: "map here, show the school".
Run Prompt 2 to turn the notes into a shot list and a maps.json file.
Run Prompt 3 to render every map shot and check it.
Drop the files on your timeline.

prompts.title: 1. Build my own map animation app (one time)
prompts.text:
Build me a small Tauri desktop app for map animations. I can't code, so keep it simple and explain how to run it.
Input: a JSON file with places (name, lat, lng), an optional route, and a theme (colours, font, pin style).
Map: free map tiles, street or satellite. Show the correct attribution for the tile provider on screen.
Output: an MP4 or PNG sequence at 1080x1920 and 1920x1080, with a smooth eased camera move between places, pins and labels in my theme.
Work only inside [PROJECT FOLDER]. Ask me before installing anything. When done, show me a test render with 2 places.

prompts.title: 2. Voice notes to map shot list
prompts.text:
Here are my voice notes from cutting the edit: [ATTACH AUDIO FILES OR PASTE TRANSCRIPT].
1. Transcribe them. For each note, list: timecode in the edit, place or places, what to show (pin, route, area, satellite view), and duration.
2. Find the lat/lng for each place. Never invent a location. If a place is unclear or has two matches, ask me.
3. Save it as maps.json: {shots:[{id, places:[{name,lat,lng}], route, style: "satellite" or "street", dur}]}.
Show me the shot list as a table and wait for my OK.

prompts.title: 3. Render and check the maps
prompts.text:
Render every shot in maps.json with my map app. Size: [1080x1920 / 1920x1080]. Frame rate: [30] fps. Theme: [COLOURS, FONT].
Check each one:
- labels readable at phone size and inside the safe area
- place names spelled exactly as in my notes or the official source
- tile attribution visible
Name files map_<shot id>_<place>.mp4 and give me the list in order with timecodes.

notes: Check the tile provider's terms and give attribution (OpenStreetMap, Esri, etc.).
Google Earth Studio is free for satellite flyovers. Render there and composite.
I still cut the A-roll myself. That's the story.
